summary: Warm the route database before asserting on it
details: The result-API case resolved the application client only inside the route. A transient connect failure could make the development fallback serve the in-memory database, so the route could not see the fixture and the test failed with a confusing authorisation-style error. Resolve the application client in the test and assert the fixture is visible before exercising the route, so a real connectivity failure fails loudly instead of degrading silently. Refs #28.

summary: Regenerate the public changelog snapshot
Record closed-ballot certification and the bound tally
details: Document that certification requires a closed ballot, that unbound votes and unreadable votes are refused, that inconclusive is always an explicit override, and that amendment endorsement ballots remain officer-supplied because O2/D18 are undecided. Correct the failure table so a zero-vote unsuccessful result needs no override, refresh the tracker, known gaps and handover status, and point the agent guide at the corrected Terms section. Refs #28.

summary: Correct the terms to describe computed ballot outcomes
details: Terms of Use §9 claimed Engage "does not calculate or apply a passing threshold", which is no longer true. Describe the versioned simple-majority-d9-v1 rule, the tie and zero-vote result, the treatment of abstentions, the absence of quorum or turnout, and the explicit, reasoned and audited override. The acceptance gate stays inactive: the document remains owner-authorised with no effective date. The incorrect sentence was in the Terms of Use, not the Privacy Policy, so the Privacy Policy and its version are unchanged. Roll the Terms to version 1.1 and record the correction and the #40 follow-up in the privacy review. Refs #28, #40.

summary: Cover closure, the bound set and override integrity
details: Close fixtures exactly as the scheduler does before certifying, and pin the override rule in the two pre-existing suites by asserting the refusal when the reason is removed rather than only supplying one. Add replica-set cases for a live ballot that cannot be certified and the changed closed tally that is then certified, a vote on another revision or with no revision, amendment-ballot votes excluded from the matter tally, an unreadable encrypted vote, missing decryption keys, an over-length override reason and a retry that rewrites the recorded reason. Cover the form focus/announcement behaviour and the PDF computed/override rows. Refs #28.

summary: Show the enforced tally and recorded outcomes
details: Derive the admin outcome basis from the same bound tally that certification enforces, so a page can no longer show a tally the server will not count. A zero-vote ballot reads "No votes yet — outcome not yet computable" instead of "Unsuccessful", and an unbound or unreadable tally is named instead of guessed. An open ballot shows when voting closes instead of an unusable result form; once a result exists both admin surfaces render the recorded outcome, computed result, tally and override reason instead of a re-submittable form. Revealing the override field moves focus to it and announces the requirement to assistive technology. Show overridden outcomes in Ballots & decisions with the reason available, and add the computed result, rule basis and override to the proposal PDF report. Refs #28.

summary: Certify only a closed ballot from a consistent bound tally
details: Refuse certification while a ballot can still accept votes. A result is accepted when the ballot has a closure marker, its close time has passed, or the system has already closed it; a live ballot returns BALLOT_NOT_CLOSED and a ballot with no recorded close is refused rather than assumed closed, because a later vote could contradict an early certification. Tally only votes bound to the ballot and exact revision, and treat the rest as a ballot defect instead of ignoring them: unbound or mismatched-revision votes now return BALLOT_TALLY_UNBOUND_VOTES, unreadable encrypted votes return BALLOT_TALLY_UNREADABLE, and missing or invalid decryption keys return BALLOT_DECRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE (503). The tally query reads only the fields the check needs. Reject an override reason longer than 1000 characters instead of truncating audit evidence, and treat a retry that changes the recorded override reason as a conflict rather than an idempotent success. The refusal message now names the computed outcome and says that any other result, including inconclusive, requires a written reason. Refs #28.

summary: Regenerate the public changelog snapshot
Record computed ballot outcome validation
details: Describe the computed Yes-versus-No check, its `simple-majority-d9-v1` basis, the stored tally and the audited override in the lifecycle, API and agent guides. Mark known gap 10 as partly resolved and keep #28/L1 Partial because the abstention denominator (O1), quorum and ranked choice remain undecided.

summary: Cover computed outcomes, overrides and stored evidence
details: Add rule-level cases for approval, rejection, a tie, zero votes and abstention-heavy ballots, plus the two admin form behaviours that reveal and require an override reason. Add real-MongoDB replica-set coverage for the parts that prove persistence and the ordered result write: the tally and rule basis stored on the result, rejection of a contradiction without a reason, an audited override, idempotent retries, refused replacement, encrypted-ballot certification through the decryption path, and a historical result that stays readable and unrewritten. The result API is exercised end to end with the dev session. Refs #28.

summary: Validate recorded outcomes against the bound tally
details: Record a formal ballot outcome only after comparing the officer's result with the outcome computed from the votes bound to that ballot and immutable revision (#28). The comparison is deliberately limited to what the decision register settles: Yes greater than No approves and a tie does not (D9); abstentions are recorded and excluded rather than given a denominator (D10, O1); no quorum, turnout or minimum-participation threshold applies (D8). The basis is versioned as `simple-majority-d9-v1`. A contradicting result is refused unless the officer supplies a written reason, and is then stored as an explicit override. The result keeps the tally at certification, the rule basis and the computed result; the `decision.recorded` event records the actor, reason, computed result and recorded result alongside the existing atomic result and ballot certification. Identical retries remain idempotent, conflicting replacements are refused, and historical results are returned unchanged and never rewritten. Both admin result forms now show the computed outcome and its tally before submission and require the override reason when the chosen result contradicts it, using the shared Field, Textarea and Badge primitives.

summary: Make the ballot_results index migration preflighted and recoverable (#55) (#83)
details: * feat(ballots): make the ballot_results index migration explicit and recoverable Startup no longer creates or drops the ballot_results indexes as a silent side effect. A legacy collection is reported and left untouched; a fresh one still receives the indexes; an already-migrated one is a no-op. `npm run ballots:results-index` adds preflight, dry-run, apply, verify and recovery commands. Apply backs up the index definitions and documents before change, proves the unique partial ballotId index before dropping the legacy unique proposalId index, verifies the final state, and records the actor and backup in data_migrations. Failures are recorded and re-raised instead of being swallowed. Duplicate results are reported for human reconciliation; nothing deletes or rewrites ballot results to make an index fit. Tests: eight replica-set cases cover a fresh install, legacy startup, duplicate blockers, dry run, full apply, partial apply, re-run, loud failure and recovery reporting. The Sprint 1 integrity test now asserts the explicit contract rather than the old startup upgrade. Also records PR #51 as merged to main and the resolved migration risk (#55). Closes #55 * chore(changelog): record the ballot-results index migration * docs(security): record Turnstile as merged to main

summary: RFC 0001: Sprint 1 integration, Phase 1 lifecycle, rendering performance and Turnstile (#51)
details: * docs(rfc): propose platform evolution and integrity programme * fix(governance): enforce ballot deadlines, rebinding, atomic decisions, and deletion guards (#26, #50) * fix(membership): guard CRM-sourced memberships, exempt national row from conflict, and record manual provenance (#32) * fix(rbac): consolidate permission enforcement, ballot binding gate, and ratification authority checks (#27, #31) * fix(proposals): clear provenance without a conflicting stage update Staff editing a proposal through the admin form always submits provenance: null for the default 'clear provenance' option. saveProposal placed provenance in both $set and $unset, which MongoDB rejects with a path conflict, so every staff edit failed against a real database. Make the clear and set branches mutually exclusive and cover the case against the real MongoDB voting suite. * fix(ballots): keep the deadline banner hydration-stable The ballot deadline rendered a server date and a post-mount relative time in the same text nodes. React 19 reported a text hydration mismatch on every ballot with a deadline, forcing an unnecessary client re-render. Mark the two intentionally time-dependent nodes as hydration-stable and make the date helper's timezone explicit so server and client markup match before the viewer-local deadline replaces it. * test(rbac): reconcile Sprint 1 authority expectations after integration The governance branch made ballots.bind and a future closing date mandatory when entering Decide, and refuses deletion of matters with governance history. The RBAC branch assumed neither. Align the fixtures with real session permissions, supply a ballot deadline, and delete a draft with no history. Ignore branch grants for permissions the catalogue reserves to National scope, allow branch-scoped comment moderation, and prove that a branch proposals.delete grant does not confer destructive authority. * docs(rfc): integrate Sprint 1 and record maintainer decisions Add the canonical governance decision register, the RFC 0001 programme tracker and the Sprint 1 integration report. Update the documentation index and replace the open-question list with the decisions now supplied, while keeping genuinely unresolved questions explicit. Add a browser verification script for the deadline, voting and vote-change journeys and record its evidence. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the Sprint 1 integration * docs(rfc): track active workstreams and new implementation issues Record the Phase 1, rendering-performance and Turnstile workstreams, link the new issues for performance (#52), the command layer (#53), the decision record and responsibility queue (#54), and ballot-results migration safety (#55). Clarify that #36 is deferred rather than blocked inside this programme. * docs(rfc): correct membership workstream status The CRM branch did not add the unique branch-membership index or the duplicate-resolving migration required by #32, so I3 remains partial. * feat(lifecycle): second proposals and schedule advancement and ballot closure Implements the approved lifecycle schedule from the decision register (D3-D7, RFC 0001 Phase 1, refs #26 and #30). - A verified member who is not the author may second a proposal while it is in Propose. The act records `secondedBy`, `secondedAt` and `deliberationEndsAt` (30 days) and writes `proposal.seconded`. It does not change the stage or grant ballot authority. - `src/lib/lifecycle-schedule.ts` is the single source of truth for the 30-day deliberation period, 30-day ballot period and 60-day ceiling. - A system actor (`system:lifecycle-scheduler`) advances due deliberations to Decide, binding the latest immutable revision and setting `ballotClosesAt = secondedAt + 60 days`. It requires no `ballots.bind`; the human early-advancement gate is unchanged. - Advancement fails closed on unresolved amendments (`rejected`, `withdrawn`, `applied`, `not-endorsed` and `inconclusive` are the only non-blocking statuses), on votes bound to other wording, on a missing seconding anchor, and on a ceiling already in the past. - Ballots close automatically at their deadline: `ballot.closed` is recorded once, the stage and result are untouched, and voting is refused after the boundary (D12 is not implemented). - Conditional filters, deterministic event IDs and transactional writes make both operations idempotent and safe under concurrent runs. - An officer opening a ballot without a date now receives the 30-day default; explicit dates remain authoritative. - Adds a read-only report for legacy ballots without deadlines and matters in Deliberate without a deliberation clock. * feat(ops): add governance scheduler and deadline migration report commands - `npm run governance:scheduler` runs the lifecycle scheduler as a dry run by default and writes only with `--apply`. It prints a JSON report with advanced, skipped, closed, blockers and errors, and exits non-zero on errors. - `npm run governance:migration-report` prints the read-only legacy report. - Both require MONGODB_URI and fail loudly without it; neither adds a daemon nor requires production credentials. * docs(lifecycle): document seconding, scheduled transitions and closure Records the implemented behaviour and the assumptions visible for review: - one seconder who is not the author; seconding records the clock but does not change the stage or gate Propose -> Deliberate; - automatic proposal advancement at the deliberation deadline by a system actor, without `ballots.bind`; - the conservative blocking-amendment set, reason codes and failure behaviour; - automatic closure at the ballot deadline without a stage change or result; - the 30-day default for officer-opened ballots; - new proposal fields (`secondedBy`, `secondedAt`, `deliberationEndsAt`, `ballotClosedAt`), deterministic event IDs and scheduler transaction rules; - the read-only migration report and its manual recovery options. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the Phase 1 lifecycle work * docs(lifecycle): state that returning to Propose keeps the seconding clock * chore(changelog): include the lifecycle documentation commits * feat(security): verify Turnstile tokens for unauthenticated actions Add server-side Cloudflare Turnstile verification (D32) and a shared MongoDB fixed-window limiter for the abuse-prone unauthenticated routes. - protect Sense Box submission, magic-link sign-in/first registration, and email sign-up if it is enabled later - fail closed with 503 and an operational error when production requires Turnstile but the secret or site key is missing - report missing, invalid, expired, replayed and malformed tokens with plain-language errors; never log or return the secret or token - store only a keyed hash of the client address, with a TTL index, so limits are shared across instances - leave authenticated voting, deliberation and admin writes untouched - tests cover configuration states, verification outcomes, route refusal and acceptance, real-MongoDB concurrency and the voting exemption * feat(security): show the Turnstile widget on protected forms Render Cloudflare Turnstile on the Sense Box and magic-link sign-in forms using Horizon primitives. The widget renders nothing when no site key is configured, reports load and expiry failures inline with a retry action, and asks for a fresh token after a rejected submission because tokens are single-use. * docs(security): document Turnstile enforcement and rate limits Record the protected actions, configuration contract, fail-closed states, failure messages, privacy boundary, rate-limit defaults and remaining gaps (CSP and headers stay with #38). Add the new keys to the environment example. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for Turnstile abuse protection * docs(security): name the rate-limit collection plainly * perf(tooling): add rendering performance harness and DB command metrics Adds an opt-in MongoDB command monitor (disabled unless ENGAGE_DB_COMMAND_MONITOR=1 and APP_MODE is not production), a development-only diagnostics route, and a repeatable Playwright/Mongo measurement harness with baseline and comparison modes. No production behaviour changes. * perf(proposals): batch independent detail reads and defer ballot hydration Runs supersede, eligibility, related-branch and evidence reads with the rest of the proposal-detail batch instead of in sequence. The ballot hydrates on idle rather than blocking load; the stance selector does the same. * perf(auth): resolve a session once per request render Layouts and pages each asked for the same session. Cache the in-flight resolution against the Request object so one browser request performs one session lookup while role revocation remains request-scoped. Adds a regression test for reuse. * perf(lists): project list reads and reuse member vote queries Stops list queries returning detailHtml and, where no search depends on it, long rationale text. Home and the proposals list reuse one member-vote read for outstanding ballots; the member page loads shared activity inputs once instead of twice. Member-page islands in inactive views hydrate only when visible. Adds visibility and vote-reuse regression tests. * perf(admin): consolidate register reads and defer participation panel The proposals register now reads the proposal collection once and batches amendment and revision lookups instead of issuing one query per row. The overview's recent-participation panel moves to a server island with a stable fallback, so its session-dependent reads no longer block the dashboard. Admin timelines hydrate when visible; migrations hydrate on idle. * perf(client): defer notification hydration off the critical path The header notification bell and notification preferences hydrate when the browser is idle. The bell is secondary to page content but still loads its unread count; no API or preference behaviour changes. * docs(status): record the rendering performance audit and measurements Classifies initial, deferred and interaction-only data per audited page; records baseline and after medians, queries removed or deferred, bundle findings, limitations and the highest-value remaining work. Adds a pnpm/npm perf:render entry point. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the rendering performance slice * fix(admin): render saved values in select controls Astro renders React component slot children as raw HTML, so React never sees the options inside NativeSelect and cannot apply defaultValue. Every select rendered its first option, which meant editing a proposal could silently reset its stage, clearing provenance, changing a member's status to pending, or applying the wrong filter or sort. Mark the stored option as selected at each affected call site. The admin proposal editor and register, member administration, Sense Box review, engagement period, policy filters and public proposal filters are covered. * feat(proposals): make seconding the act that opens deliberation D3 requires a seconder before Deliberate and D4 anchors the clock to seconding. The initial Phase 1 implementation recorded the seconding but left Propose -> Deliberate to an officer, which could stall a proposal indefinitely and run the clock in the wrong stage. Seconding now performs the transition and records both the seconding and the stage transition. Officer and API transitions into Deliberate are refused without a recorded seconder. A member-facing control appears on the proposal page for eligible, non-author members, with inline feedback and no raw controls. Update the unrelated stage-transition fixtures to record a seconder explicitly. Extend the browser verification to cover seconding, the 30-day default when no ballot date is given, a rejected past date, and the editor showing the proposal's real stage. * docs(lifecycle): record Phase 1 delivery and the remaining decisions Mark seconding, scheduled advancement and automatic closure as implemented, update the known-gap register, and add O9/O10 for the administrative direct-creation path and renewed seconding after material rewrites. * chore(changelog): refresh after the rendering performance merge * docs(rfc): record Phase 1, rendering performance and Turnstile integration Update I2, I6, I10, I12 and the workstream table with measured evidence and the remaining gaps. Mark the performance and Turnstile documents as merged into the integration branch. * docs(rfc): mark integrated workstreams and the next Phase 2 slices * docs(rfc): add the Phase 2 orchestrator handover brief Record the handover state, governance invariants, traps found during delivery, the recommended Phase 2 sequence, parallelisation rules, verification commands, open decisions and the first ten actions for the next orchestrator. * fix(security,proposals): address PR #51 review findings * chore(deploy): pass Turnstile and rate-limit env vars to app container * fix(governance,security,ui): address CodeRabbit review findings on PR #51 * test(rate-limit): align future window assertions in real MongoDB test

The page previews each additive migration, shows the last recorded run and any error, and applies Standard branches or Branch participation individually or in order. Every run is recorded in data_migrations with run count, timestamps, actor and result. Standard branches is an idempotent seed for Fusion National, VIC, NSW, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, ACT and NT with National as parent; existing branches are never renamed, re-parented or un-recognised. Branch participation remains blocked until the National branch exists. The command-line seed now uses the same service, and the participation migration remains available for deployment automation.

summary: Record branch participation and verification
Separate branch following from verified membership
details: Members choose the branches they follow during onboarding and in My Engage. Authorised administrators verify followers as members in a focused Branch governance workspace. Branch subscriptions are now Engage-owned preferences, while verified organisational membership stays in branch_memberships with source, verification and audit metadata. National governance is included for every verified account and never removed by branch preferences. Existing members without branch connections receive national scope silently and a one-time state branch invitation. Eligibility is decided in one service used by proposal pages, ballot submission, pending-vote promotion and digests. Followers can discover branch activity but cannot vote. Revocation requires a reason and preserves historical votes and the person's following preference. The migration backfills legacy membership metadata, adds subscriptions without duplicating them, assigns open proposals without branch context to national governance, and leaves branch-owned and archived records untouched. The Underground CRM boundary is implemented through applyExternalMembership: external membership facts can update organisational membership but never branch subscriptions, and local administrators cannot silently override CRM-sourced records. Tests cover national defaults, follow/unfollow idempotency, source integrity, permissions, migration, parent/child eligibility and new proposal defaults.
